blurb: Central skate park in the city that is lit until 10 pm, for skateboards, scooters and rollerblades.

name: Weston Creek Skate Park
blurb: Weston skate park, lit until 10 pm, for skateboards, scooters and rollerblades.

name: Eddison Park
blurb: Woden park with a public disc golf course, plus a skate park, play equipment, fitness stations and an orienteering course.

name: Casey Dog Park
blurb: Fenced off-leash dog park on Springbank Rise, one of the ACT's official fenced dog parks.

name: Belconnen Dog Park
blurb: Fenced off-leash dog park at Diddams Close on Lake Ginninderra, with an off-leash dog swimming beach nearby.

name: Yarralumla Dog Park
blurb: Fenced dog park on Bank Street beside Weston Park, with off-leash swimming spots at Kurrajong Point and Orana Bay nearby.

name: Swamp Creek
blurb: Murrumbidgee picnic area popular with birdwatchers for rainbow bee-eaters and birds of prey; dogs welcome off leash unless signed.

name: National Library of Australia
blurb: Indoor: browse the Treasures Gallery and the Papunya Literature Production Centre exhibition, then sit in the grand Main Reading Room.

name: National Archives of Australia
blurb: Indoors, see free exhibitions of Australian history, including the Holden collection, in the heritage-listed East Block building.

name: Museum of Australian Democracy at Old Parliament House
blurb: Indoor: walk the old Senate and House chambers and the Prime Minister's suite, with guided tours and hands-on craft and dress-up for kids.

name: National Film and Sound Archive
blurb: Indoors, catch classic and arthouse double features and free screenings in the heritage Arc Cinema, plus archive exhibitions.

name: Royal Australian Mint
blurb: Watch coins being made through the factory windows and try the hands-on exhibits; family-friendly and mostly indoors.

name: Canberra Museum and Gallery
blurb: Indoor: local history and art in the heart of Civic, including the Nolan Gallery and changing free exhibitions.

name: Mount Stromlo Observatory
blurb: Stargaze through telescopes on a public astronomy night with talks, or see a space film in the old dome, on the hill above Weston Creek.

name: Lanyon Homestead
blurb: Wander the historic homestead and gardens near Tharwa, with garden tours and seasonal events.

name: Calthorpes' House
blurb: Step inside a 1920s family home preserved with its original furniture and garden, on a guided Saturday-afternoon tour.

name: Canberra Railway Museum
blurb: See vintage locomotives and carriages at a volunteer-run railway museum; good for train-loving kids.

name: Government House
blurb: Tour the Governor-General's residence and grounds on a free open day, with self-guided access to the house and gardens.

name: Gorman Arts Centre
blurb: Wander the heritage arts precinct for galleries, studios, workshops, dance and music classes, and one-off performances.

name: Ainslie Arts Centre
blurb: Community arts hall for markets, dance nights, book launches and band rehearsals, including the Craft + Design Canberra design market.

name: The Shine Dome
blurb: Take a half-hour tour inside the Academy of Science's iconic dome, open to the public on its annual open day.

name: High Court of Australia
blurb: Walk into the cavernous public hall and sit in on a court sitting; the building is free and open to visitors on weekdays.

name: National Capital Exhibition
blurb: Free lakeside exhibition on how Canberra was designed and built, with maquettes, photos and film; Indoors, just off the lake path.

name: Blundells Cottage
blurb: Peek into a small farm cottage on the lake shore and see how a working family lived before Canberra existed.

name: National Carillon
blurb: Sit on the lakeside lawn and hear a free bell recital from the lakeside tower, with a blanket and a picnic.

name: Queanbeyan Museum
blurb: Poke through volunteer-run displays on Queanbeyan's history, free to enter on weekend afternoons.

name: Belconnen Arts Centre
blurb: Lakeside arts centre with changing galleries, workshops, a theatre and a cafe; open Tuesday to Sunday.

name: Tuggeranong Arts Centre
blurb: South Canberra's arts hub for free gallery shows, jazz after work, comedy nights and workshops.

name: M16 Artspace
blurb: Artist-run gallery with a new show every few weeks, open Wednesday to Sunday afternoons, free to wander through.

name: Craft + Design Canberra
blurb: Browse handmade ceramics, jewellery and design in the Civic gallery and shop, with exhibitions by local makers.

name: PhotoAccess
blurb: Photography gallery and darkroom in the Manuka Arts Centre, with a rolling program of free exhibitions.

name: Gallery of Small Things
blurb: A tiny artist-run gallery in a Watson backyard showing miniature paintings, ceramics and small works, free entry.

name: Megalo Print Studio and Gallery
blurb: Printmaking studio with a gallery of local print shows; handy before or after the Sunday Old Bus Depot Markets.

name: Canberra Contemporary
blurb: Lakeside contemporary art space with experimental shows; the Takeaway exhibition anchors the 2026 Canberra Art Biennial.

name: Platform by Canberra Contemporary
blurb: Small street-front gallery beside the Manuka shops, showing emerging and First Nations artists, easy to drop into.

name: ANU School of Art and Design Gallery
blurb: University art gallery hosting the Drill Hall Gallery's shows while it is closed, plus the annual graduate exhibition.

name: Canberra City Public Art Walking Trail
blurb: Follow a self-guided route of sculptures and murals through Civic, from Ethos to Ainslie's Sheep; three route lengths.

name: Tuggeranong Public Art Trail
blurb: A lakeside walk past public sculptures, with a kids' brochure that turns it into a trail with the Firestorm Story Tree.

name: Mill Theatre at Dairy Road
blurb: Indoors, catch plays up close in an intimate 67-seat studio in the Dairy Road precinct.

name: Canberra Repertory Theatre
blurb: Community theatre company staging classic and modern plays in its own theatre near the lake.

name: The Q Queanbeyan Performing Arts Centre
blurb: A short drive east for theatre, music, dance and comedy, with touring shows and local companies.

name: ACT Hub
blurb: Independent theatre in the heritage Causeway Hall, run by three companies, with a different play every month or two.

name: Llewellyn Hall
blurb: Big concert hall at ANU for orchestras, Musica Viva, jazz and student concerts, many of them free.

name: Wesley Music Centre
blurb: Classical and chamber concerts in a church hall, plus lunchtime recitals; small and intimate.

name: Gang Gang Cafe and Bar
blurb: Suburban cafe-bar with gigs, jazz jams, comedy and trivia, plus Latin and folk nights.

name: Fun Time Pony
blurb: Underground Civic venue with local bands, stand-up comedy and a dance floor, plus pizza.

name: The Baso
blurb: Underground Belconnen venue (formerly The Basement) for touring bands and packed gigs.

name: The Pot Belly
blurb: Belconnen pub with rock gigs and acoustic nights.

name: The George Harcourt Inn
blurb: Local pub with live music on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, backing up-and-coming local talent.

name: Molly
blurb: Cocktail bar with live jazz most nights, from solo piano on Tuesdays to a Chicago-style jam on Wednesdays.

name: Shadows Night Club
blurb: DJs and bands playing post-punk, darkwave, goth and industrial in Civic.

name: Harmonie German Club
blurb: Club room with local, interstate and international acts, and the odd market.

name: Canberra Irish Club
blurb: Friday-night local bands and monthly traditional Irish music in a family-friendly club.

name: UC Refectory
blurb: University hall hosting national and international bands across genres, with new lineups each month.

name: White Eagle Polish Club
blurb: Polish club with local and international acts, acoustic sets and band nights.

name: Rose Cottage
blurb: Gilmore venue with local acts, indoors by the fire or out in the courtyard.

name: Sunset Cinema at the Botanic Gardens
blurb: Outdoor movies on a summer evening on the Eucalypt Lawn; bring a picnic and a rug.

name: Dendy Cinemas Canberra
blurb: Indoors, see films on the IMAX screen, plus festival screenings and opera, ballet and theatre broadcasts, in the Canberra Centre.

name: Exhibition Park in Canberra (EPIC)
blurb: Showgrounds hosting the National Folk Festival, Royal Canberra Show, Summernats and the Handmade Market.

name: National Convention Centre
blurb: Canberra's largest events venue, hosting major touring concerts and conferences in Civic.

name: Handmade Market Canberra
blurb: Quarterly market of 250-plus makers selling ceramics, jewellery, art and gifts across several indoor pavilions.

name: Haig Park Village Markets
blurb: Sunday market under the pines with stalls, food and coffee; pair it with a walk through the park.

name: Southside Farmers Market
blurb: Sunday-morning farmers market with fresh produce and baked goods at Canberra College.

name: Hartley Hall Markets
blurb: Monthly village market at Hall Showground with handmade goods, plants, food and coffee.

name: The Little Burley Market
blurb: Monthly lakeside market beside Lake Burley Griffin with local makers and treats.

name: Sly Fox Market
blurb: Monthly lakeside market on Emu Bank with stalls for gifts, art and clothes.

name: Fyshwick Fresh Food Markets
blurb: Long-running covered food market with produce, meat, seafood and flowers, open Thursday to Sunday.

name: Lakeside Markets Tuggeranong
blurb: Monthly southside market at Lake Tuggeranong College with makers and food stalls.

name: Trash and Treasure Market Jamison
blurb: Sunday-morning trash and treasure market in the Jamison car park for second-hand finds.

name: Murrumbateman Village Market
blurb: Craft, produce and local wine stalls on the village green, with a cafe on site; a short drive up the Barton Highway.

name: Bungendore Farmers Market
blurb: Regional meat, veg, honey and eggs sold by growers in the village square, with cafes and a wine bar nearby.

name: Strathnairn Arts
blurb: Homestead galleries, studios, a shop and a cafe in a 1920s homestead on the city's western edge, with Brindabella views.

name: Zone 3 Laser Tag
blurb: Indoors: laser tag in a labyrinth arena with computerised vests and handheld lasers, played in short rotations by anyone aged six and up.

name: Jet Flight Simulator Canberra
blurb: Indoors: take the captain's seat of a Boeing 737-800NG simulator with an instructor and up to four passengers, in 30 to 120 minute sessions.

name: Missing Klues Escape Rooms
blurb: Indoors: story-driven escape rooms for groups, with a 60-minute clock, a performance breakdown and a drink afterwards.

name: Escape Rooms Canberra
blurb: Indoors: high-production escape rooms attached to a garden cocktail bar, so you can unwind with a drink after the puzzles.

name: Hijinx Hotel
blurb: Indoors: 15 team challenge rooms to race through against the clock, plus a bar, inside the Canberra Centre.

name: MANIAX Axe Throwing
blurb: Learn to hurl hatchets with a coach, then compete in a mini tournament, with craft beer and stone-baked pizza on site.

name: Axxe
blurb: Axe throwing at digital targets with real-time scoring, plus party-style mini games such as beer pong and zombie hunt.

name: Breakr Smash Room
blurb: Suit up and smash plates, mugs and glassware (sourced from op shops) in an enclosed room with your own music; ages 14 and over.

name: iPlay Belconnen
blurb: Indoors: laser tag, ten-pin bowling, drift dodgem cars, pool tables and over 80 arcade games under one roof in Westfield Belconnen.

name: Canberra Racquet Club
blurb: Book a court for padel (six courts) or pickleball (four) at a 4,000 square metre club with a cafe and bar; open to the public.

name: Status Golf
blurb: Indoors: hit real balls into simulator screens to play more than 200 famous courses, with a sports bar attached.

name: P59 Golf
blurb: Indoors: TrackMan simulator bays on Emu Bank overlooking Lake Ginninderra, with PGA coaching and a putting green.

name: Splash Lab
blurb: Indoors: suit up and fling paint at canvases in a splatter-paint studio; no artistic skill needed.

name: Pinot and Picasso Belconnen
blurb: Indoors: paint-and-sip nights where a host walks you through a canvas step by step, with weekly public sessions.

name: Instala DIY Studio
blurb: Indoors: beginner-friendly workshops such as perfume making, candle making and mosaic lamps, BYO drinks welcome.

name: Australian Dance Party Classes
blurb: Indoors: weekly bookable dance classes in Open, Mover and Advanced levels; the Open class needs no dance experience.

name: Funland Canberra
blurb: Indoors: giant jungle gym, soft play and interactive toys for children of all ages, with a cafe for parents; no booking needed.

name: Let's Play Indoor Playground & Cafe
blurb: Indoors: slides and climbing structures plus a baby and toddler zone, with a healthy cafe on site.

name: Little Amigos
blurb: Indoors: play zones with slides, train rides and a ball pool for little kids, inside the Canberra Outlet.

name: Sprouts Corner Indoor Playcentre
blurb: Indoors: a nature-inspired play centre and cafe for children aged 0 to 7 and their families.

name: Inflatable World Kambah
blurb: Indoors: a completely inflatable playground where kids can bounce and climb out of the sun.

name: Lollipop's Playland & Cafe
blurb: Indoors: a play centre with a dedicated toddler area and plenty for older kids, with a cafe for parents.

name: Flip Out Majura
blurb: Indoors: a 2,000 square metre trampoline park with foam pits, a parkour area, arcade games and party rooms.

name: Yarralumla Play Station
blurb: Four acres of hedge mazes and the Infinity Room, mini golf of Canberra icons, farm animals and a miniature railway by the lake.

name: Canberra Reptile Zoo
blurb: Meet reptiles, frogs and native animals up close, with keepers on hand and some animals you can touch.

name: Canberra International Golf Centre
blurb: Two-storey driving range open till late, plus an 18-hole pitch and putt and a mini golf course.

name: Floating Sauna Lake Burley Griffin
blurb: Wood-fired saunas on a floating pontoon with lake views, with a dip in the lake or a cold shower on deck between rounds.

name: Jindii EcoSpa
blurb: Day spa treatments built around native botanical ingredients, in a garden setting inside the Botanic Gardens.

name: Yoga Paws Puppy Yoga
blurb: Weekend 60-minute beginner-friendly yoga with puppies roaming nearby; sessions alternate between Phillip and Narrabundah, ages 12 and over.

name: Beltana Farm Truffle Hunts
blurb: Follow truffle dogs through the oak plantation and pull a truffle from the ground, then a long lunch or a hands-on cooking class; truffle season only.

name: Wine Hopper Murrumbateman
blurb: Hop-on, hop-off chauffeured day tour of the Murrumbateman cellar doors, so nobody has to drive.

name: Balloon Aloft
blurb: Sunrise hot air balloon rides over Canberra, daily and weather dependent, from the city's original balloon operator.

name: Paranormal Investigations at Old Parliament House
blurb: After-dark ghost hunt through the heritage rooms and corridors of Old Parliament House, using ghost-hunting tools and spirit communication.

name: Wine Tasting and Stargazing at Mount Majura
blurb: An hour tasting six wines with cheese and charcuterie, then an hour of guided stargazing with an astronomer, minutes from the city.

name: Love Boats Canberra
blurb: Walk-up hire of licence-free electric boats or pedal boats on Lake Burley Griffin, from three lakeside locations.

name: GoBoat Canberra
blurb: Self-drive electric picnic boat for up to eight with a table on board; no boat licence needed and dogs are welcome.

name: The Paddle Hub
blurb: Stand-up paddle board and kayak hire on Yarralumla Bay run by the YMCA; seasonal October to April and by group booking.

name: Canberra Miniature Railway
blurb: Ride miniature steam, electric and petrol trains around about 1.5 km of track on public running days held twice a month.

name: Treetops Adventure Canberra
blurb: Outdoor treetop courses in Majura Pines with 90 obstacles and 16 ziplines, two to twenty metres up, for ages three and up.

name: Delta Force Paintball
blurb: Outdoor paintball on movie-set style fields, with MiniBall for kids from ten and standard paintball from sixteen.

name: Forest Park Riding and Equitation School
blurb: One-hour trail rides for beginners to advanced riders aged seven and up, with lessons and school-holiday programs, 20 minutes from the city.

name: Canberra Walk-in Aviary
blurb: Walk through a planted aviary of nearly 600 birds and feed the free-flying parrots; entry includes a plate of bird food.

name: VR Canberra
blurb: Indoors: virtual reality games and VR escape rooms for groups, in Mitchell.

name: Zone Bowling Belconnen
blurb: Indoors: ten-pin bowling with a Timezone arcade next door, a good wet-weather group outing in Belconnen.

name: Dickson Pool
blurb: Outdoor summer pool with a 50 m pool, heated learners pool, toddler pool and splash park; reopened for the season on 31 October 2026.

name: Manuka Pool
blurb: Seasonal outdoor public pool in Manuka, reopened for the warmer months on 24 October 2026.

name: Canberra Olympic Pool
blurb: Outdoor Olympic pool in the city centre with toddler and dive pools in summer, reopened for the season on 1 November 2026.

name: Gungahlin Leisure Centre
blurb: Indoors: public swimming pool and leisure centre in Gungahlin, open all year round with group fitness and swim lessons.

name: Lakeside Leisure Centre
blurb: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre in Tuggeranong, open all year round.

name: Erindale Leisure Centre
blurb: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre in the Erindale Centre, open all year round with group fitness classes.

name: Stromlo Leisure Centre
blurb: Indoors: public pool and leisure centre at Stromlo Forest Park, open all year round.

name: Queanbeyan Aquatic Centre
blurb: A 25 m indoor pool all year, plus a 50 m outdoor pool and wet play area from October to March.

name: Clonakilla
blurb: Taste shiraz viognier at the cellar door of the region's first modern vineyard, by the fire in winter or on the vineyard-view patio in summer.

name: Helm Wines
blurb: Riesling tastings in an 1888 National Trust schoolhouse, run by the family that has made wine here since 1973.

name: Shaw Estate
blurb: Seated four or six wine tastings in a modern cellar door, with a Mediterranean restaurant on site; a long lunch for a group.

name: Collector Wines
blurb: Guided cool-climate tastings in the restored Hazeldean building in Collector village, about 40 minutes from Canberra.

name: Tallagandra Hill
blurb: Winery with a concert programme: live gigs among the vines, plus cellar door tastings for groups booked in advance.

name: McKellar Ridge Wines
blurb: Small family cellar door where the owners pour cool-climate wines themselves on weekends.

name: Yarrh Wines
blurb: Rammed-earth cellar door with western views and low-intervention wines; tastings, charcuterie or a two-course lunch.

name: The Vintner's Daughter
blurb: Guided tastings in the cellar door or on the verandah; early arrivals can join morning feeding time with the farm animals.

name: Pankhurst Wines
blurb: Estate-grown wines with some of the region's best views, poured by the owners about 20 minutes from Canberra.

name: Heywood Cellar Door and Restaurant (Nick O'Leary)
blurb: Guided tastings at the bar, then a farm-to-table restaurant meal paired with Nick O'Leary wines, with Brindabella views.

name: Lerida Estate
blurb: Pinot noir and shiraz with views over Lake George, with Cafe Lerida and cheese boards on site.

name: Mount Majura Vineyard
blurb: Guided tastings in a cellar door overlooking the vines, only 15 minutes from the city; a winter truffle tasting runs with The Truffle Farm.

name: Poachers Pantry Smokehouse and Vineyard
blurb: Splash tastings, a smokehouse restaurant and a farm shop with coffee, all on a working farm near the Murrumbateman wine region.

name: Brindabella Hills Winery
blurb: Weekend wine by the glass on the terrace or a set-menu lunch above the Murrumbidgee, 25 minutes from the city.

name: Lark Hill Winery
blurb: Biodynamic cool-climate winery at 860 m with a courtyard cellar door and weekend restaurant service.

name: Lake George Winery
blurb: Boutique pinot noir and chardonnay with lunch Wednesday to Sunday on a 300-acre vineyard, with tiny-home stays.

name: Norton Road Wines
blurb: Family cellar door in Wamboin pouring small-batch pinot noir and riesling, with a BBQ restaurant close by.

name: Gallagher Wines
blurb: Family cellar door where winemaker Greg Gallagher often pours his sparkling and riesling, with cheese and preserves on sale.

name: Eden Road Wines
blurb: Cool-climate wines tasted at a cellar door 30 minutes from the city, on the Barton Highway side of Murrumbateman.

name: Murrumbateman Winery
blurb: One of the region's oldest wineries (1973); riesling and shiraz tastings daily, dog and child friendly.

name: Surveyors Hill Vineyards
blurb: Women-run vineyard with a cellar door and bistro open weekends, with accommodation on the property.

name: Sapling Yard Cellar Door
blurb: Italian-style wines poured at a reclaimed-timber bar in Bungendore village, with cheese boards from Scrumpers Kitchen next door.

name: Gundog Estate Cellar Door
blurb: Dog-friendly tastings in the renovated stables of the Royal Hotel, with lunch from the neighbouring Grazing restaurant.

name: Contentious Character Urban Cellar Door
blurb: Canberra District wines tasted in town; the cellar door moved here from the Wamboin vineyard. Indoors.

name: Canberra Cellar Door
blurb: Saturday pop-up where six Canberra District wines are poured by the lake, a quick tasting without driving out to Murrumbateman.

name: Win's Creek Meadery
blurb: Taste honey mead flights, cider and craft beer in an 1879 inn, with pizza and a honey shop; one of few meaderies around Canberra.

name: The Canberra Distillery
blurb: Small-batch gin, whisky and rum made on site, with a cellar door and shop for tastings. Indoors.

name: Big River Distilling Co
blurb: Craft gin distillery in the Dairy Road precinct with weekend tours and tastings of three spirits. Indoors.

name: Ambrosia Distillery and Lounge
blurb: Flavoured vodka and native-botanical gin from a Dairy Road distillery, with a cocktail lounge next door. Indoors.

name: Underground Spirits
blurb: Canberra gin distillery with a cellar door, plus a seasonal Floriade Gin Garden. Indoors.

name: Lager House by Capital Brewing Co
blurb: Neighbourhood pub pouring tank-fresh lagers from three tanks, with a wood-fired grill kitchen. Indoors, good for a group.

name: Majura Valley Farm
blurb: Farm gate shop with eggs, vegetables, flowers and lamb, and an autumn sunflower maze that families walk through.

name: Blackwattle Alpaca Farm
blurb: Book a walk and hand-feeding with alpacas and llamas, then browse the yarn shop and cafe.

name: Blue Frog Truffle Farm
blurb: Join a family-run truffle hunt with dogs on Sundays in the mid-June to mid-August season, 5 km from the ACT border.

name: The Truffle Farm
blurb: Winter truffle hunt among an oak forest 15 minutes from the city, as a hunt, brunch or degustation.

name: Turalla Truffles
blurb: Bungendore truffle growers selling fresh truffles and hosting a degustation lunch in winter.

name: Tanbella Orchard
blurb: Pick your own apples, pears and nashi on an autumn day, a short drive from the city; open late January to May only.

name: O'Connor Dog Park
blurb: Fenced off-leash dog park in the inner north with separate yards for big and small dogs, agility gear, benches and shade.

name: Duffy Dog Park (Weston Creek)
blurb: Fenced dog park with separate large- and small-dog areas, dirt, grass and woodchip to run on, a shade sail and benches.

name: Greenway Dog Park (Lake Tuggeranong)
blurb: Dog park beside Lake Tuggeranong with big eucalypts for shade, open grass, benches and two play areas split by dog size.

name: Forde Dog Park
blurb: Fenced dog park inside Forde Heritage Park with agility hoops, hurdles and pipes; barbecues, a playground and trails are next door.

name: Franklin Dog Park
blurb: New fenced off-leash park with an agility area, grassed space for fetch, a small shelter and dog-waste bag dispensers.

name: Lanyon Dog Park
blurb: Fenced off-leash park opened Nov 2025, with separate grass areas for small and large dogs, agility gear, a shelter and a drinking fountain.

name: Farrer Nature Play & Adventure Trail
blurb: Nature-based play and adventure trail where kids climb, crawl and explore; one of the ACT Government's favourite play spots in Woden Weston Molonglo.

name: Ruth Park Playground
blurb: Playground by Holden's Creek Pond in Coombs with a water pump kids can play with on a warm day.

name: Joey Park Playground
blurb: Neighbourhood playground on Bettong Avenue in Throsby, picked in the ACT Government's list of favourite play spots in Gungahlin.

name: Ridgeline Park
blurb: Ridge-top playground in Denman Prospect with climbing nets and tunnels, and outdoor fitness equipment in the same park.

name: Denman Village Park Splash Pad
blurb: Splash pad opposite the Denman Prospect shops with several fountains of different sizes, handy on a hot day.

name: Forde Heritage Park
blurb: Shaded playground with swings, slides and climbing frames, a covered picnic area, toilets and a trail lined with outdoor fitness equipment.

name: Wildbark Nature Play Space
blurb: Nature play beside the Mulligans Flat visitor centre with concrete tunnels, a fallen tree to climb and log steppers.

name: Callum Brae Nature Reserve
blurb: Quiet woodland reserve known as a birdwatching hotspot for threatened woodland birds, with marked walking tracks; no dogs.

name: Farrer Ridge Nature Reserve
blurb: Gentle ridge between the Woden and Tuggeranong valleys, popular for walking, running and cycling; dogs on leash on tracks.

name: Gossan Hill Nature Reserve
blurb: Small hill reserve in south-east Belconnen with a 2.5 km loop and unusual rock formations; dogs on leash.

name: Gungaderra Grasslands Nature Reserve
blurb: Grassland reserve rising to wooded Gungahlin Hill, dotted with old scribbly gums, with quiet management trails to walk.

name: McQuoids Hill Nature Reserve
blurb: Small hill reserve in the west of the Tuggeranong Valley with views of the Murrumbidgee River; the National Trail follows its western edge.

name: Nadjung Mada Nature Reserve
blurb: Woodland and grassland reserve in eastern Gungahlin where Superb Parrots feed in breeding season; quiet walking and birdwatching.

name: Percival Hill Nature Reserve
blurb: Reserve beside Ginninderra Creek with rare wildflowers and orchids; walk the tracks with a dog on leash.

name: Tuggeranong Hill Nature Reserve
blurb: A steep track climbs to the summit for views over the Tuggeranong Valley and the Bullen Range.

name: Wanniassa Hills Nature Reserve
blurb: Short ridge walk with sweeping views of southern Canberra, good birdwatching and spring wildflowers.

name: Crace Grasslands Nature Reserve
blurb: Grassland reserve that rises to the rocky Crace Hill knoll at 622 m, with grassy tracks for a quiet walk; no dogs.

name: Budjan Galindji Grasslands Nature Reserve
blurb: Small grassland and woodland reserve in Franklin where migratory Latham's Snipe visit the seasonal wetlands.

name: Justice Robert Hope Park
blurb: Flat low woodland of scattered mature trees on the lower slopes of Mount Majura, an easy bush stroll in the inner north.

name: Barrer Hill walks (Molonglo River Reserve)
blurb: Easy 1.8 km Barrer Circuit plus a short summit track on Barrer Hill, with wide views over the Molonglo River Reserve; bikes allowed.

name: Mount Rogers Reserve
blurb: Short, easy and popular 2 km loop in the northern suburbs; a quick bush walk close to Belconnen.

name: Church Rock Heritage Loop
blurb: A 2.5 km loop of about an hour at Tidbinbilla past the Flints homestead site and Church Rock.

name: London Bridge Walk
blurb: A 4.5 km circuit at Googong Foreshores out to a heritage-listed natural rock arch and the London Bridge Homestead site.

name: Mount McDonald Summit Track
blurb: Moderate 3.8 or 5.2 km return walk of two to three hours to a summit with views back over Canberra.

name: Shepherds Lookout
blurb: Short 1.2 km return walk from Stockdill Drive to a lookout over the Murrumbidgee River; dogs may run off leash here.

name: One Tree Hill Walk
blurb: Longer walk of about 8.5 km return from near Hall up One Tree Hill, rewarded with wide views over the north.

name: Uriarra Loop
blurb: A 3.5 km walk along sandy Murrumbidgee River banks with views; allow two to two and a half hours.

name: Mindjagari Track
blurb: Roughly 26 km network of difficult management trails and walking tracks in Namadgi that can be linked into longer routes.

name: Namadgi Visitor Centre Woodland Walk
blurb: Easy 1 km loop through grassy woodland from the Namadgi Visitor Centre, with displays on Gudgenby and an Aboriginal scarred tree.

name: Brandy Flat Walk
blurb: A 10 km return walk from Glendale Crossing through box woodland and dry forest to Brandy Flat Hut; the southern half is steep.

name: Birrigai Time Trail
blurb: A walk at Tidbinbilla that tells the culture and history of the Ngunnawal people, including a rock shelter.

name: Lennox Gardens
blurb: Lakeside gardens with a red gravel boulevard to the water, the Canberra Beijing Garden, free barbecues and outdoor fitness gear.

name: Dairy Farmers Hill Lookout
blurb: 360-degree views over Canberra from the top of Dairy Farmers Hill, with the eagle sculpture Nest III and a picnic table.

name: Regatta Point Lookout
blurb: Grassy hill overlooking Lake Burley Griffin with toilets and picnic shelters, a handy lakeside spot for a picnic.

name: National Rose Gardens
blurb: Spring rose displays, wisteria on pergolas and shady lawns next to Old Parliament House, good for a picnic.

name: Woden Town parkrun
blurb: Free weekly timed 5 km run or walk every Saturday at 8 am in Woden Town Park beside Yarralumla Creek, with no road crossings.

name: Tuggeranong parkrun
blurb: Free weekly 5 km run or walk on the Lake Tuggeranong foreshore from Tuggeranong Town Park; a fairly flat out-and-back.

name: Gungahlin parkrun
blurb: Free weekly 5 km run or walk around the flat loop of Yerrabi Pond, open to joggers, walkers and parkrun regulars.

name: Burley Griffin parkrun
blurb: Free weekly 5 km parkrun at Weston Park beside Lake Burley Griffin, open to runners, joggers and walkers.

name: Umbagong District parkrun
blurb: Free weekly 5 km parkrun at Umbagong District Park in Latham, starting a short walk from parking at the Kippax shops.

name: Wagi Bridge parkrun
blurb: Free weekly 5 km parkrun in Gungahlin, two laps of the shared path around the Wagi Bridge footbridge.

name: Athllon Park Disc Golf Course
blurb: Free public disc golf course in Athllon Park; play solo or with friends, with course info from the ACT Disc Golf Club.

name: Eddison Park Skatepark
blurb: One of the ACT's seven major skateparks, for skateboarders and scooter riders of all levels; lit until 10 pm.

name: Yerrabi Skatepark
blurb: Major skatepark beside Yerrabi Pond for skateboarders and scooter riders of all levels; lit until 10 pm.

name: Warehouse Circus
blurb: Circus classes from tumbling and acrobalance to aerials, for ages from tiny tots to adults.

name: Corin Forest
blurb: Alpine slide down a 1.2 km forest track in summer, snow play and beginner snow slopes in winter, about 45 minutes from the city.

name: Majura Valley Farm Sunflower Maze
blurb: Wander the sunflower maze in March on the ACT's oldest working farm, ten minutes from the city; the farm gate shop is open daily.

name: Quizzic Alley
blurb: Indoors: Harry Potter-themed shop that runs layered potion-making classes for kids in the school holidays.

name: Canberra Archery Club
blurb: Beginner come-and-try archery with coaches and equipment provided at the city's oldest archery club.

name: Cycle City Hire (Stromlo Forest Park)
blurb: Hire a full-suspension mountain bike or a toddler balance bike at Stromlo Forest Park on weekends; a shuttle runs up the mountain.

name: Gold Creek Country Club
blurb: Public-access 18-hole par 72 golf course designed by Bruce Devlin, with a grassed driving range and hire clubs.

name: Woden Gardenland
blurb: Indoors: soft play for ages 1 to 6 with climbing, crawling and sliding among Canberra-themed artwork.

name: MarketQuest
blurb: Indoors: slides plus rope and agility platforms for kids, inside Marketplace Gungahlin.

name: Ninja Parc
blurb: Indoors: ninja-style obstacle course for ages 6 and up, soft play for under 8s and climbing walls.
